newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude diffs flat, prices up with WTI.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude diffs flat, prices up with WTI.

text.p: Discounts for U.S. West Coast crudes were unchanged midday Tuesday, while outright prices continued to firm with West Texas Intermediate.
October deliveries of Alaska North Slope remained at $2.15 a barrel off West Texas Intermediate, with further weakness forecast by buyers.
Meanwhile, WTI was seen firmer amid bullish technicals and reports that Iraq was massing troops in the south.
WTI October was seen $24.15/24.25 a barrel, 45 cents over late Monday levels.
A number of refinery outages, both planned and unplanned, kept distillate prices firm, but failed to affect crudes, traders noted.

A gasoline-making unit at Chevron's El Segundo plant was slated to come off line at the end of September, and coker and crude units at Texaco's Los Angeles refinery were due down this week, traders said.
Kern River was quoted at discounts of around 35/25 cents to posted pricings at $15.75 a barrel.
Values for Wilmington stood at $17.00/17.20 a barrel, while Line 63 differentials were unchanged at WTI minus $2.60/2.50 a barrel.
